scenario: 招聘人在电话中途说：「说实话，我们现在还没到能从 Meta/TikTok 这种级别招人的阶段。」这是一个软拒绝信号。
scenario_en: Mid-call the recruiter says, "Honestly, we're not hiring at the Meta/TikTok level yet." It's a soft-rejection signal.
q: 听到这句软拒绝，下一步最该怎么做？
q_en: What's the right next move when you hear this soft rejection?
options: 当作没听见，假装那句软拒绝不存在，顺着他的话继续答下一个技术问题，指望级别的顾虑自己会过去
顺着他点头：「嗯，可能我确实更适合更成熟一点的团队」，然后主动把话题岔到别的项目上去
直接接住并重定级别：「我不是来要 senior 头衔的——你描述的 PSP 集成、税务、checkout 正是我想端到端 own 的活，我冲的是问题不是级别。」
反驳他：「我在 Meta/TikTok 带过更大的 scope，这个级别对我其实偏低了」，坚持自己配得上更高职位
tradeoff: 正面接住 vs 假装没听见：假装能躲开当场那点尴尬，代价是对方带着「不匹配」的结论挂断电话。
why: 软拒绝必须当场正面接住，并把级别重新框成「我要的就是这摊活」——我冲的是问题不是头衔。装作没听见，通话结束时对方只会认定我不匹配。
why_en: Address a soft rejection head-on and reframe the level right away — I'm here for the problem, not the title — because ignoring it ends the call with them sure I misfit.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实只想要更高级别的岗位、不愿降级做这摊活时，才该顺着「级别不够」结束——那说明这个岗位本就不适合你。
options_en: Pretend the soft rejection didn't happen, keep answering his next technical question, and hope the level concern just passes.
Nod along — "Yeah, maybe I'm a better fit for a more established team" — and then steer the topic to a different project.

Address it head-on and reframe the level: "I'm not here for a senior title — the PSP, tax, and checkout work you described is exactly what I want to own end-to-end. I'm here for the problem, not the level."
Push back: "I've owned bigger scope at Meta/TikTok, this level is actually low for me," insisting you deserve a higher role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方看你没接信号，通话结束时默认你不匹配。
等于替对方把自己淘汰，白丢一个机会。
对方从「你太 senior」松动为「他要的就是这活」，软拒绝被你当场接回。
坐实 over-positioned 的顾虑，把软拒绝推成硬拒绝。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see you missed the signal and close the call assuming you misfit.
You disqualify yourself for them and throw away a real chance.
They shift from "too senior" to "this is the work he wants" — you catch the soft no in the moment.
You confirm the over-positioned worry and push the soft no into a hard no.

scenario: 招聘人用整整 2 分钟介绍了岗位：数字支付产品、PSP 集成、税务处理、checkout、tap-to-pay。现在轮到你做 self-intro。
scenario_en: The recruiter just spent two full minutes describing the role: digital payments, PSP integrations, tax handling, checkout, tap-to-pay. Now it's your turn to self-intro.
q: 你的 self-intro 该怎么开头？
options: 挑他刚说的一个信号反射回去：「你说的 PSP 集成和 checkout，正好对上我在 Meta 做的从商家输入到后端的多步骤数据流，我想在支付方向深入。」
从最早的实习开始，按时间顺序把简历从头到尾讲一遍，指望对方自己听出哪一段跟这个支付岗位相关
直接开讲你最自豪的 Promotion Day 项目，细节拉满，却完全不提它跟 PSP、checkout 有没有关系
先反问一句「能再把这个岗位的职责和技术栈说一遍吗」，用澄清把开场的主动权交回给对方
tradeoff: 先反射信号 vs 直接背简历：背简历省掉当场读岗位的功夫，代价是开场没有连接，对方得自己猜你合不合适。
why: 先反射对方刚描述的一个具体信号，再桥接到能对上的项目——先说连接点，再说简历。开局若是流水账，对方感觉不到你和这个岗位的关系。
why_en: Reflect back one concrete signal they just described, then bridge to a matching project — lead with the connection, not a chronological resume dump.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方完全没描述岗位、直接说「介绍下你自己」时，才用一段结构化的背景概述来开头。
options_en: Reflect one signal back: "The PSP and checkout work you described maps to the multi-step data flow I built at Meta from business input to backend — I want to go deeper on payments."
Start from your earliest internship and walk the resume chronologically to now, hoping they figure out which part relates to this payments role.
Launch into your proudest project (Promotion Day) in full detail, never tying it to PSP or checkout at all.
First ask, "Could you repeat the role's responsibilities and stack?" — using clarification to hand the opening back to them.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻感到你听懂了岗位，也看到你背景对得上。
信息量大但零连接，对方要自己去猜你合不合适。
项目再强，跟支付无关就显得你没在听。
把主动权交回去，浪费了展示连接的黄金开场。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They immediately feel you understood the role and see your fit.
Lots of info, zero connection — they have to guess whether you fit.
A strong but off-topic project reads as "not listening."
You hand control back and waste the opening's chance to show fit.

scenario: 对方刚花两分钟描述完岗位/产品，接着说「介绍下你自己吧」。你要用一个能连接岗位的 self-intro 回应。
scenario_en: They just spent two minutes describing the role/product, then say "tell me about yourself." You want a self-intro that connects to the role.
q: 把「连接岗位的 self-intro」四步排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four steps of a role-connected self-intro in the correct order.
steps: 桥接到一个能对上这个信号的、你自己做过的项目
完整听完对方对岗位/产品的描述，先不急着开口
点出你最想在这个方向深入的地方，把话头留给对方
从他的描述里挑一个具体信号，用一句话反射回去
why: 顺序是先听、再反射一个具体信号、再桥接到我的项目、最后留一个想深入的钩子——连接永远排在简历前面。
why_en: The order is listen fully, reflect one concrete signal back, bridge to my matching project, then leave a hook — the connection always comes before the resume.

q: 面试前，每个要提到的项目该准备好哪三件技术底细？
q_en: For each project you'll mention, which three technical details must you have ready?
text: 每个会在面试里提到的项目，提前准备三件事：(1) 数据在{{后端}}怎么存，(2) {{前端}}怎么把更新发过去，(3) {{schema}} 大概长什么样。
text_en: For each project you'll mention, prep three things: (1) how data is stored on the {{backend}}, (2) how the {{frontend}} sends updates, (3) what the {{schema}} looks like.
why: 我在 self-intro 里提了 Meta onboarding，却答不出步骤状态怎么存——那是我自己的项目。每个要提的项目都先备好这三件，追问就不会卡。
why_en: I described my own Meta onboarding project but couldn't say how step state was stored — prep backend storage, frontend update path, and schema for every project I'll mention.

scenario: 你在 self-intro 里描述了 Meta 的多步骤 onboarding 流程；面试官追问：「那每一步的状态是怎么存的、怎么传给后端的？」你其实没背过这块。
scenario_en: In your self-intro you described Meta's multi-step onboarding flow; the interviewer follows up, "How was each step's state stored and sent to the backend?" — and you hadn't rehearsed that part.
q: 这一刻，什么才是根本的修复（而不是当场找补）？
q_en: In this moment, what's the real fix (not an on-the-spot patch)?
options: 现场即兴编一套听起来合理的存储方式和数据流，赌面试官不会继续往下追问
含糊地挡回去：「这块得翻代码才能确认」，把这个追问推开、不正面接
把话题硬拉回项目的业务影响和上线指标，绕开他问的那个技术细节
认清根因：自己项目也要会前备好「后端怎么存 / 前端怎么更新 / schema」，这样追问不会卡
why: 这是我自己的项目却答不上存储方式，很尴尬。真正的修复不在现场，而在会前——每个要提的项目都把存储、更新路径、schema 背熟。
why_en: Blanking on how my own project stored state is embarrassing; the real fix is before the call — rehearse storage, update path, and schema for every project I'll mention.
whenOtherWins: 只有当追问的是一个你确实没参与、边界之外的模块时，「这块不是我负责、我需要看下代码」才是诚实且合适的答法。
options_en: Improvise a plausible-sounding storage and data-flow story and bet he won't keep digging.
Vaguely deflect — "I'd have to check the code to confirm this part" — and push the follow-up away instead of facing it.
Force the topic back to business impact and launch metrics to sidestep the exact technical detail he asked about.
Recognize the root cause: pre-rehearse "how it's stored / how the frontend updates / the schema" for your own projects so follow-ups don't stump you.
optionScenarioImpacts: 编错了会被追问戳穿，比承认更糟。
对自己主导的项目说这话，像是没真正做过。
绕开只会让面试官觉得你答不上核心细节。
指向会前准备，这是唯一能根治「卡在自己项目上」的做法。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A wrong guess gets exposed on follow-up, worse than admitting.
Saying this about a project you led reads as if you didn't really build it.
Dodging just signals you can't answer the core detail.
Points to pre-call prep, the only real cure for freezing on your own project.

scenario: 这已经是第五次面试被问「为什么离开 TikTok」。之前你在不同公司给过不同方向——有时说「端到端 ownership、更接近客户」，在一家 VC 电话里又说「深入基础设施平台和可靠性」。
scenario_en: This is the fifth interview asking "why are you leaving TikTok." Across companies you've given different directions — sometimes "end-to-end ownership, closer to the customer," but on a VC call "go deeper into infra platform and reliability."
q: 该怎么处理这个反复出问题的答案？
q_en: How should you handle this repeatedly-fumbled answer?
options: 每家公司临场即兴，挑当下听起来最顺的方向说
定一个真实且一致的方向（端到端 ownership、更接近客户痛点），每次都这么说，练到自动
看岗位是平台还是产品——平台就说 infra、产品就说 ownership
干脆说得模糊些（「想成长、想学新东西」），避免自相矛盾
tradeoff: 固定一个方向 vs 见人下菜：临场换方向听着灵活，代价是招聘人一交叉比对，方向漂移就露馅。
why: 招聘人网络会互相对信息，方向反复会露馅。选一个真实的方向——端到端 ownership、更接近客户痛点——每次一致，练到脱口而出。
why_en: Recruiter networks compare notes, so pick one true direction — end-to-end ownership, closer to customer pain — and say it consistently until it's automatic.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实在专门投基础设施岗位时，才该整体切到 infra 方向——但也要全程只用那一个方向，不能来回混。
options_en: Improvise per company, picking whatever direction sounds smoothest in the moment.
Fix one true, consistent direction (end-to-end ownership, closer to customer pain) and drill it until automatic.
Switch by role — say infra for platform jobs, ownership for product jobs.
Keep it vague ("want to grow, learn new things") to avoid contradicting yourself.
optionScenarioImpacts: 方向漂移，招聘人一对信息就觉得你没想清楚。
一致的真实方向，重复越多越可信、越流畅。
两条职业路径混着说，等于告诉对方你自己没定。
模糊答案没有说服力，也留不下记忆点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Drifting direction reads as "hasn't figured it out" when recruiters compare.
One consistent true direction gets more credible and fluent with repetition.
Mixing two career paths tells them you haven't decided.
A vague answer persuades no one and leaves no memory hook.

q: 「why startup」的答案里，比「end-to-end ownership」更具体的那句升级短语是什么？
q_en: In the "why startup" answer, what's the upgrade phrase that's more concrete than "end-to-end ownership"?
text: 「why startup」比「end-to-end ownership」更具体的升级说法是：{{tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain}}——强调工作离真实问题更近，而不只是 own 得更多。
text_en: The upgrade over "end-to-end ownership" for the why-startup answer is: {{tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain}} — the work sits closer to a real problem, not just owning more.
why: 「end-to-end ownership」太泛，升级成「工作和客户痛点之间更紧密的连接」——在大公司一个小改动要 5 个团队、3 个月对齐，我想直接看到这种连接。
why_en: "End-to-end ownership" is vague, so upgrade it to a tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain — in a big org a small change means five teams and three months of alignment.

scenario: 面试快结束，面试官问「你有什么想问我的吗？」这是你连续第六次面试走到这一步。
scenario_en: The interview is wrapping up and the interviewer asks, "Any questions for me?" This is the sixth interview in a row you've reached this point.
q: 前五次你都没问出实质问题——这次该怎么做？
q_en: You asked nothing substantive the last five times — what should you do now?
options: 笑着说「你介绍得很全面，我要问的其实都覆盖到了，暂时没有问题」，就此把反问环节收掉
只问流程性的问题：面试还有几轮、大概什么时候出结果、下一步是谁来面
随口抛一个谁都能问的泛问题，比如「公司文化怎么样？团队氛围好不好？」
问两个会前写在纸上的实质问题（如：团队现在最大的、还没定的技术决策是什么？工程师怎么直接接触客户反馈？）
why: 连续六次没问实质问题已成模式。每次会前把两个实质问题写在纸上，不管通话怎样都问出来——这是显示我认真评估岗位的地方。
why_en: Six interviews with no real questions is a pattern; write two substantive questions on paper before every call and ask them no matter how the call went.
whenOtherWins: 如果你原本想问的两个问题在前面聊天里都已被自然回答，就现场追一个更深的后续问题，而不是硬套清单。
options_en: Smile and say, "You covered everything really well — the things I'd ask are already answered, so no questions for now," and close the round out.
Only ask process questions: how many rounds are left, roughly when you'll hear back, who's interviewing next.
Toss out a generic question anyone could ask, like "What's the company culture like? Is the team a good vibe?"
Ask two substantive questions written on paper beforehand (e.g., the biggest open technical decision the team faces; how engineers get direct customer feedback).
optionScenarioImpacts: 「没问题」读作没兴趣或没准备。
只问流程，显得你对这份工作本身不好奇。
泛泛问题任何人都能问，留不下印象。
有备而来的实质问题，显示你认真在评估这个岗位。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "No questions" reads as no interest or no prep.
Process-only questions signal no curiosity about the work itself.
A generic question anyone could ask leaves no impression.
Prepared substantive questions show you're seriously evaluating the role.

scenario: 你问了团队结构，面试官给了很实在的回答（30 人、7 名工程师、扁平层级、每个工程师都直接和客户交流）。现在轮到你接话。
scenario_en: You asked about team structure and got a real answer (30 people, 7 engineers, flat hierarchy, every engineer talks to customers directly). Now it's your turn again.
q: 得到这个好答案后，接下来最该做什么？
q_en: After getting that good answer, what's the best next move?
options: 顺着深挖一个实质后续问题：「你说工程师直接和客户交流——通常怎么发生的？是陪着参加销售电话，还是通过产品反馈异步进行？」
顺势点点头，然后转去问流程性的问题：面试还剩几轮、结果大概什么时候出、下一步谁来面
只回一句「明白了，听起来挺有意思」，就把反问环节收掉，没有接着往下追
跳到一个跟刚才回答完全无关的新话题，比如薪资、假期或者能不能远程办公
tradeoff: 深挖一层 vs 退回流程：直接收口省事，代价是等于告诉对方「我没别的想问了」，好奇心没展示出来。
why: 一个好问题后面跟着流程问题，读起来就是「我问完了」。真正的好答案值得顺着再深挖一层，展示我在认真消化对方说的话。
why_en: One good question followed by a process question reads as "I ran out"; a strong answer deserves a deeper substantive follow-up that shows I'm actually engaging.
whenOtherWins: 如果时间确实快到、面试官已经在收尾，那用一个简短的流程/下一步问题收口是合适的。
options_en: Dig one layer deeper with a substantive follow-up: "You said engineers talk to customers directly — how does that usually happen? Sitting in on sales calls, or async through product feedback?"
Nod along, then switch to process questions: how many rounds are left, when you'll hear back, who's interviewing next.
Just say "Got it, that's interesting" and wrap up the questions without going any deeper.
Jump to a topic unrelated to their answer, like salary, vacation, or whether remote work is allowed.
optionScenarioImpacts: 顺势深挖，显示你真在思考对方的回答。
退回流程问题，暴露「我没别的可问了」。
太快收口，浪费了一次展示好奇心的机会。
跳到无关话题，显得没在听刚才的答案。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Going deeper shows you're truly engaging with their answer.
Retreating to process exposes "I have nothing else to ask."
Closing too fast wastes a chance to show curiosity.
Jumping topics reads as not having listened to the answer.

scenario: 面试快结束，面试官抛来一个开放问题：「你希望团队记住你什么？」这家 Alex AI 做 AI 招聘系统；你在 Meta 做过 AI onboarding，在 TikTok 做过面向广告主的规模化产品界面。
scenario_en: At the close, the interviewer asks an open question: "What would you want the team to remember you for?" Alex AI builds an AI recruiter; you built AI onboarding at Meta and an advertiser-facing scaled product interface at TikTok.
q: 这个开放收尾问题，怎么答最好？
q_en: How do you best answer this open closing question?
options: 给一句泛泛的热情：「我真的很期待能加入、和你们一起努力工作、快速成长，成为团队的一份子。」
打「快速学习」牌：「我是个学得很快的人，不管什么技术栈、什么领域，给我一点时间都能很快上手。」
一个具体连接：「我已经做过你们需要的两面——Meta 的 AI onboarding，和 TikTok 规模化的用户端产品界面，我不是来学这些的。」
谦虚地说自己还有很多东西要学、经验也许还不够，但保证会非常拼、加班加点也要补上来
tradeoff: 具体连接 vs 泛泛热情：热情谁都会说，代价是转身就被忘，你已具备的匹配一点没留下。
why: 这个开放问题是礼物，别退回泛泛的热情。用一个具体连接——我已经做过你们需要的两面（AI 层 + 用户端产品），不是来学的——才会被记住。
why_en: This open question is a gift; don't default to generic enthusiasm — leave a specific connection (I've already built both sides you need) that they'll actually remember.
whenOtherWins: 如果你和这个岗位的连接确实不强，那与其硬编一个假连接，不如诚实说你最想快速补上的一块——但那也说明这家匹配度本就不高。
options_en: Offer generic enthusiasm: "I'm really excited to join, work hard with you all, grow fast, and be part of the team."
Play the fast-learner card: "I pick things up quickly — whatever the stack or domain, give me a little time and I'll be up to speed."
A specific connection: "I've already built both sides you need — Meta's AI onboarding and TikTok's scaled user-facing product. I'm not here to learn those."
Humbly say you still have a lot to learn and maybe not enough experience, but you'll work extra hard and put in the hours to catch up.
optionScenarioImpacts: 泛泛热情，任何候选人都能说，转身就忘。
「学得快」回避了这个展示具体价值的机会。
具体连接留下记忆点，直接对上他们的需求。
强调不足反而弱化了你已具备的匹配。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Generic enthusiasm any candidate could say, forgotten instantly.
"Fast learner" dodges the chance to show specific value.
A concrete connection sticks and maps straight to their need.
Emphasizing gaps undercuts the fit you already have.

scenario: 面试官在 42 分钟处暂停对话，说「你每道题前都停顿很久」，并问你是不是在用 AI；她说技术轮会上检测。
scenario_en: At minute 42 the interviewer paused the call to say "you pause a lot before every answer" and asked if you were using AI, adding that detection will be added in technical rounds.
q: 每题前长时间停顿、被怀疑用 AI——标准修复是什么？
q_en: Long pauses before every answer that trigger an AI suspicion — what's the standard fix?
text: 停顿感 / AI 嫌疑的修复：面试前做 {{10}} 分钟出声预热，凭记忆、计时回答 {{3-4}} 个问题；如果用笔记，只写{{关键词}}（如「trade-offs: speed vs safety」），不要写整句。
text_en: Fix for the pausing / AI-perception flag: a {{10}}-minute out-loud warmup before the call, answering {{3-4}} questions from memory and timed; keep notes as {{single keywords}}, not full sentences.
why: 有没有真用 AI 不重要，长停顿的模式让人觉得我在读 AI。会前 10 分钟出声预热，把答案先流起来；笔记只留关键词，不然会照着念。
why_en: Whether or not AI was used, the long-pause pattern looks like reading from a bot, so warm up out loud for ten minutes and keep notes as keywords, not sentences.

q: Meta 外面的人听不懂「HAC」「PRAC」——面试里该分别说成什么？
q_en: Outsiders don't understand "HAC" or "PRAC" — what should you say instead in an interview?
text: 面试里别说 Meta 内部黑话：把「HAC」说成 {{PHP 后端}}（Hack 是 PHP 派生的服务端语言），把「PRAC」说成 {{React 前端}}。公司名可以说，内部项目代号不行。
text_en: Don't say Meta-internal jargon in interviews: say {{PHP backend}} instead of "HAC" (Hack is a PHP-derived server language), and {{React frontend}} instead of "PRAC". The company name is fine; internal codenames are not.
why: 「HAC」「PRAC」是 Meta 内部对 Hack 和 React 的缩写，外面的人听到是乱码。说「PHP 后端」「React 前端」，对方一听就懂。
why_en: "HAC" and "PRAC" are Meta-internal shorthand for Hack and React that sound like gibberish outside; say "PHP backend" and "React frontend" instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 内部用的一种 PHP 派生的服务端语言；对外说「PHP 后端」更好懂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hack is Meta's PHP-derived server-side language; say "PHP backend" so outsiders understand.

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么想来我们公司？」这家 Alex AI 做的是 AI 招聘系统。你在 Meta 做过 AI onboarding，在 TikTok 做过面向广告主的复杂工作流界面。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks "Why do you want to work here?" Alex AI builds an AI recruiter. You built AI onboarding at Meta and an advertiser-facing complex-workflow interface at TikTok.
q: 「为什么选这家公司」怎么答才到位？
q_en: How do you answer "why this company" well?
options: 给一串对任何创业公司都成立的通用理由：「我就是喜欢创业公司——product focus、团队小、节奏快、能端到端 own 一个东西。」
点一个具体产品事实连到你真做过的东西：「AI 招聘系统要 AI 层 + 面向用户的产品——正好是我在 Meta 做的 AI onboarding 和 TikTok 的广告主界面这两条腿。」
夸他们的融资和团队规模：「你们刚融完一轮、团队还在扩，势头很好，我觉得前景不错、很想上车。」
「我一直想进 AI 这个方向，你们做的正好是 AI，我觉得挺契合的，很想加入你们团队一起做。」
tradeoff: 具体产品事实 vs 通用创业理由：通用理由对每家都成立，代价是零区分度，证明不了你为这家做过功课。
why: 「product focus、team 小、end-to-end」对任何创业公司都成立，等于没说。要点一个具体产品事实，连到我真做过的东西——这才证明我为这家做了功课。
why_en: "Product focus, small team, end-to-end" is true of any startup and says nothing; name one specific product fact and connect it to something I actually built.
whenOtherWins: 如果这家公司你确实只被通用的创业属性吸引、找不到具体连接点，那可能说明匹配度不够——但至少该在会前研究出一个具体事实。
options_en: Give reasons true of any startup: "I just love startups — product focus, small team, fast pace, owning something end-to-end."

Name a specific product fact and connect it to what you built: "An AI recruiter needs an AI layer plus a user-facing product — exactly the two legs of my Meta AI onboarding and my TikTok advertiser interface."
Praise their funding and team size: "You just raised a round and the team's still growing — there's real momentum, the outlook looks great and I want in."
"I've always wanted to move into AI, and you happen to do AI, so it feels like a good fit and I'd love to join the team and build with you."
optionScenarioImpacts: 通用创业理由，对方听过一百遍，零区分度。
具体产品事实 + 真实经历，证明你研究过也匹配。
夸融资规模跟你能做什么无关，留不下印象。
「你们做 AI」太泛，没连到你具体做过什么。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A generic startup reason they've heard a hundred times, zero differentiation.
A specific product fact plus real experience proves research and fit.
Praising funding says nothing about what you can do.
"You do AI" is too vague and connects to nothing you built.

scenario: 这是一个 VC 的 sourcing 电话——招聘人手上有 3-5 家 portfolio 公司要给你匹配，不是在筛你进某一个具体岗位。你的 self-intro 快讲完了。
scenario_en: This is a VC sourcing call — the recruiter has 3-5 portfolio companies to match you to, not one specific job to screen you for. Your self-intro is wrapping up.
q: self-intro 该用哪种框架收尾？
q_en: How should the self-intro close in this framing?
options: 给一个可匹配的画像：「我在找 early-stage AI 公司，想做最早的工程师之一、端到端 own 一个产品面，哪家 portfolio 对得上都想聊。」
像在投单个岗位那样收尾：「我在找一个能让我做 X 的后端工程师岗位」，把自己框死在一个具体职位上，让 VC 没法跨公司匹配
反过来问他们：「你们现在具体在招哪个岗位？职责、技术栈、团队是什么样的？」，把方向的皮球又踢回给对方
只顺着简历把过往经历从头到尾又讲一遍，完全不提自己想要什么阶段、什么问题域、什么方向的公司
why: VC 是在把我匹配到 3-5 家公司，不是筛一个岗位。要给可匹配的材料——公司规模、问题域、团队结构，以「我想做早期工程师、最擅长 X」收尾，而不是「我在找一个做 X 的岗位」。
why_en: A VC is matching me to several portfolio companies, so give a matchable profile — company stage, problem domain, team structure — framed as "I want to be an early hire best at X," not "I'm looking for a role that does X."
whenOtherWins: 如果这通电话其实是某家公司自己的招聘人在招一个确定的岗位，那就该针对那个具体岗位来定位，而不是给宽泛画像。
options_en: Give a matchable profile: "I'm looking for early-stage AI companies where I can be one of the first engineers and own a product surface end-to-end — whichever portfolio company fits, I'd love to talk."
Close like you're applying to one job: "I'm looking for a backend engineer role where I do X," boxing yourself into one position so the VC can't match you across companies.
Turn it around and ask them: "Which specific role are you hiring for? What are the responsibilities, stack, and team like?" — punting the direction back to them.
Just recount your past experience end to end from the resume again, without saying what stage, problem domain, or direction of company you want.
optionScenarioImpacts: 给出可匹配画像，VC 能立刻往 portfolio 里对号入座。
单岗位口径，VC 没法把你匹配到多家公司。
把匹配的主动权丢回去，VC 要的是你的画像。
只讲过去、不讲想要，VC 无从匹配。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A matchable profile lets the VC slot you against portfolio companies immediately.
Single-job framing gives the VC nothing to match across companies.
Handing matching back wastes it — the VC wants your profile.
Past-only, no wants, leaves the VC nothing to match on.
